title: A Primitive Invocation has exactly two exits: graduate to the Active Instances Directory or be archived as a failure
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.1.1.4 spells out the routing for an in-flight Invocation: the directory holds "all prospective Instances of the Executor Accord Primitive whose Invocation is currently in progress. Invocations that are completed successfully are moved to [the] Active Instances Directory, whereas failed Invocations are Archived in [the] Hub Data Repository."

Two properties follow. First, **prospective Instances are tracked before they exist as Instances** — the Atlas records intent, not just outcomes, so an observer can see what is being attempted in real time rather than only what succeeded.

Second, **there is no silent exit**. A failed Invocation is not removed from the record; it is relocated. Combined with the Suspended Instances subtree, this means the Hub Data Repository accumulates the complete negative history of a Primitive's use.

That is what makes the Primitive framework auditable in a governance sense rather than merely descriptive: an Agent cannot make an embarrassing attempt disappear by abandoning it, because abandonment has a defined destination in the document tree.
description: The In Progress Invocations Directory is a staging area, not a terminus, so every attempt leaves a permanent record in the Hub Data Repository whether or not it ever became an Instance.
